Fix \(k=(g,t)\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and \(u\in\{g,\ldots,t\}\).  Consistency gives
\[
m_{g,1,u}(X)=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(g,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X].
\tag{C1}
\]
No effect on ineligible units and consistency give
\[
m_{g,0,u}(X)=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=g,S=0,X],
\quad
m_{c,0,u}(X)=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=c,S=0,X].
\tag{C2}
\]
Because \(c>t\ge u\), mean no anticipation at \(u\) and \(u-1\), followed by consistency, gives
\[
m_{c,1,u}(X)=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=c,S=1,X];
\tag{C3}
\]
when \(c=\infty\), (C3) is immediate.  Subtracting the conditional parallel-gap equality from (C1)--(C3) yields
\[
m_{g,1,u}-m_{g,0,u}-m_{c,1,u}+m_{c,0,u}
=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(g,1)-\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X].
\tag{C4}
\]
Summing (C4) from \(g\) through \(t\) telescopes.  Mean no anticipation at \(g-1<g\) removes the lower endpoint, hence
\[
q_{k,c}(X)=E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X].
\tag{C5}
\]
Cell overlap implies \(\pi_{g,1}=E_P[p_{g,1}(X)]\ge\varepsilon>0\).  Multiplying (C5) by \(p_{g,1}(X)/\pi_{g,1}\), integrating over \(P_X\), and applying iterated expectation gives
\[
\theta_k(P)=\frac{E_P[p_{g,1}(X)q_{k,c}(X)]}{\pi_{g,1}}
=E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1].
\tag{C6}
\]
The aggregate formula follows from the definition of \(\tau_\omega\).  Finally every residual in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) has conditional mean zero, so
\[
E_P[\Psi_{k,c,P}(O)\mid X]
=\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{\pi_{g,1}}\{q_{k,c}(X)-\theta_k(P)\}.
\tag{C7}
\]
Equation (C7) is exactly the displayed denominator-corrected ratio score; it retains the derivative of \(\pi_{g,1}\).

Because \(A\) has full column rank and the columns of \(N\) are an orthonormal basis of \(\ker(A')\), every feasible vector has a unique representation \(b=b^0+Nz\).  Suppress \(x\) and put \(g=N'\Gamma b^0\).  Then
\[
(b^0+Nz)'\Gamma(b^0+Nz)
=b^{0\prime}\Gamma b^0+2z'g+z'Hz.
\tag{O1}
\]
If \(v\in\ker H\), positive semidefiniteness gives
\[
0=v'Hv=(Nv)'\Gamma(Nv)=\|\Gamma^{1/2}Nv\|^2.
\]
Thus \(\Gamma Nv=0\) and \(v'g=(Nv)'\Gamma b^0=0\).  Since \(H\) is finite-dimensional and symmetric, \((\ker H)^\perp=\operatorname{range}H\), so \(g\in\operatorname{range}H\).  The normal equation \(Hz=-g\) is solvable, and its unique solution in \(\operatorname{range}H\) is \(z^\star=-H^\dagger g\).  Hence
\[
b^\star=b^0-NH^\dagger N'\Gamma b^0,
\quad A'b^\star=\omega,
\quad N'\Gamma b^\star=g-HH^\dagger g=0.
\tag{O2}
\]
Under fixed rank and the separated positive spectrum, \(H^\dagger\) is obtained by applying the Borel function \(z\mapsto z^{-1}\mathbf 1\{z\ge\kappa\}\) to the measurable symmetric matrix \(H\); therefore (O2) is measurable.  Two minimizers differ by \(Nv\) with \(v\in\ker H\), and the preceding calculation identifies this set with \(\ker\Gamma\cap\ker A'\).

If \(\Gamma\) is positive definite, the Lagrange equations are \(\Gamma b=A\lambda\) and \(A'b=\omega\).  Full column rank of \(A\) makes \(A'\Gamma^{-1}A\) positive definite.  Solving gives
\[
b=\Gamma^{-1}A(A'\Gamma^{-1}A)^{-1}\omega.
\]

There are finitely many support points, folds, score coordinates, and retained cells.  The lower support-mass bound and overlap imply that every relevant training-cell count is of order \(n\) in probability.  Every corrected score coordinate is a finite sum of outcome residuals multiplied by propensity ratios bounded in terms of \(\varepsilon\), plus the target-share correction.  Fixed \(T\), the conditional fourth-moment envelope, and Jensen's inequality therefore give
\[
\sup_{x:P_X(x)>0}E_P[\|\Psi_P(O)\|^4\mid X=x]<\infty.
\tag{L1}
\]
Thus every coordinate of \(\Psi_P\Psi_P'\) has finite conditional variance.  Chebyshev's inequality in each cell and a union bound over the fixed collection show that the oracle conditional first and second moments, and hence the oracle conditional covariance, have error \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) simultaneously over support points and folds.

On the clipped overlap region, the maps in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) are finite sums and products, and every reciprocal propensity has derivative bounded by a constant depending only on \(\varepsilon\).  Add and subtract the oracle propensity and regression in each coordinate.  The mean-value inequality followed by H\"older's inequality gives
\[
\max_\ell\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}
\le O_P(n^{-1/2})+C\{r_{p,n}+r_{m,n}\}.
\tag{L2}
\]
All vector and matrix norms are equivalent because both the support and the score dimension are fixed.  This proves the first assertion and the claim about the remaining cell-average conditional moments.

With parametric cell first stages, (L2) gives \(r_{\Gamma,n}=O(n^{-1/2})\).  If \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), then
\[
r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n=O(n^{-1/2+a})\to0,
\qquad r_{b,n}=O(n^{-1/2+a}).
\]
Lemma \(\ref{lem:loading-perturbation}\) gives rank recovery, and
\[
r_{b,n}^2+r_{\Gamma,n}^2=O(n^{-1+2a}+n^{-1})=o(n^{-1/2})
\]
for \(0<a<1/4\).  For continuously distributed \(X\), fourth moments provide only conditional second moments for score products and provide neither a smoothness class nor the tail control needed for an \(L_4(P_X)\) nonparametric covariance rate.  Hence no such continuous-covariate rate follows.

Put \(E_\ell(x)=\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)-\Gamma(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Since \(N'N=I\), the variational characterization of ordered eigenvalues gives
\[
\max_j|\lambda_j\{N'\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)N\}-\lambda_j\{H(x)\}|
\le E_\ell(x).
\tag{B1}
\]
For all large \(n\), \(\tau_n<\kappa/2\).  A false positive from the zero cluster requires \(E_\ell(x)>\tau_n\), and a false negative from the positive cluster requires \(E_\ell(x)\ge\kappa-\tau_n>\tau_n\).  Markov's inequality and the \(L_4(P_X)\) covariance rate give, uniformly over the fixed folds,
\[
P_X\{\widehat r^{-\ell}(X)\ne r_0\}
\le\tau_n^{-4}\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}^4
=O_P\{(r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n)^4\}.
\tag{B2}
\]

By Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\), \(g=N'\Gamma b^0\) belongs to \(\operatorname{range}H\).  Set \(z^0=H^\dagger g\), so \(Hz^0=g\), and \(\widehat g=N'\widehat\Gamma b^0\).  The spectral gap and conditional fourth-moment envelope bound \(z^0\).  With \(\widehat P_\tau=\widehat H_\tau^\dagger\widehat H\), the exact identity
\[
\widehat H_\tau^\dagger\widehat g
=\widehat P_\tau z^0
+\widehat H_\tau^\dagger\{(H-\widehat H)z^0+(\widehat g-g)\}
\tag{B3}
\]
applies.  The retained inverse has norm at most \(\tau_n^{-1}\), while
\(\|\widehat H-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|\widehat g-g\|\le CE_\ell\).  If \(E_\ell\le\tau_n\), projecting the empirical eigenvector equations onto \(\ker H\), and the population equations onto the retained empirical null space, yields
\[
\|\widehat P_\tau-P_H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\frac{2E_\ell}{\kappa-E_\ell}.
\tag{B4}
\]
If \(E_\ell>\tau_n\), the trivial projector bound is at most \(2E_\ell/\tau_n\).  Since \(P_Hz^0=z^0\), (B3)--(B4) yield
\[
\|\widehat b^{-\ell}(x)-b^\star(x)\|
\le C E_\ell(x)/\tau_n.
\tag{B5}
\]
Taking \(L_4(P_X)\), and then \(L_2(P_X)\), norms proves the claimed \(O_P(r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n)\) bounds.  Threshold separation makes them \(o_P(1)\).  On the rank-recovery event the retained eigenvalues are at least \(\kappa/2\); using this bound in (B3) instead of \(\tau_n^{-1}\) gives the sharper fixed-law rate \(O_P(r_{\Gamma,n})\).

Let \(\eta=(p,m)\),
\[
\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)=K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X),
\qquad
\mu_P(O)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_kR_{k,c_0(k),P}(O).
\]
Conditional on a training complement, validation observations are independent of foldwise estimates.  For \(k=(g,t)\), write \(M_{a,s,k}=\sum_{u=g}^tm_{a,s,u}\), and let \(B_{k,c}\) be the bracketed numerator in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\).  Adding and subtracting true regressions gives the exact conditional identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[\widehat B_{k,c}-B_{k,c}\mid X]
={}&\left(\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}p_{g,0}}{\widehat p_{g,0}}-p_{g,1}\right)
(\widehat M_{g,0,k}-M_{g,0,k})\\
&+\left(\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}p_{c,1}}{\widehat p_{c,1}}-p_{g,1}\right)
(\widehat M_{c,1,k}-M_{c,1,k})\\
&+\left(p_{g,1}-\frac{\widehat p_{g,1}p_{c,0}}{\widehat p_{c,0}}\right)
(\widehat M_{c,0,k}-M_{c,0,k}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{A1}
\]
Overlap makes every coefficient Lipschitz in \(\widehat p-p\).  Fixed dimension and H\"older's inequality imply
\[
|P\{\mu(O;\widehat\eta)-\mu(O;\eta)\}|
\le C\|\widehat p-p\|_{P_X,4}\|\widehat m-m\|_{P_X,4}
=O_P(n^{-1}).
\tag{A2}
\]

Lemma \(\ref{lem:ovs-orthogonal-normal-signal}\) and the OVS equalities give
\[
\|E_P[\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}\mid X,\mathcal D_{-\ell}]\|_{P_X,2}
=O_P(n^{-1}),
\qquad S^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O;\eta)=Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O).
\tag{A3}
\]
Proposition \(\ref{prop:ovs-normal-finite-support-rates}\) gives
\[
\max_\ell\|\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}-\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\|_{P_X,4}
=O_P(n^{-1/2+a})=o_P(1).
\tag{A4}
\]
The conditional fourth-moment envelope, nuisance consistency, and (A4) yield
\[
\|\widehat\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS}}^{-\ell}(X)'\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS},-\ell}
-\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\|_{P,2}=o_P(1).
\tag{A5}
\]
Equations (A3)--(A4) also make the conditional mean of (A5) of order \(O_P(n^{-1})\).  Conditional Chebyshev inequality fold by fold, followed by summation over the fixed number of folds, gives
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_\omega(P)
=(\mathbb P_n-P)\{\mu_P-\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\}
+o_P(n^{-1/2}),
\tag{A6}
\]
apart from the empirical target-share contribution.

Overlap gives \(\pi_{g,1}>0\), and Taylor expansion of the global empirical share gives
\[
\widehat\pi_{g,1}^{-1}-\pi_{g,1}^{-1}
=-\pi_{g,1}^{-2}(\widehat\pi_{g,1}-\pi_{g,1})+O_P(n^{-1}).
\tag{A7}
\]
The expectation of the bracketed numerator for block \(k=(g,t)\) is \(\pi_{g,1}\theta_k(P)\).  Thus (A7) contributes
\[
-\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\frac{\theta_k(P)}{\pi_{g,1}}
(\mathbb P_n-P)\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=1\}+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{A8}
\]
By Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\), combining (A6) and (A8) replaces \(\mu_P-E_P\mu_P\) by \(\psi_P^0\).  Hence
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_\omega(P)\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
\{\psi_P^0(O_i)-\alpha_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X_i)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O_i)\}+o_P(1)
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(O_i)+o_P(1).
\tag{A9}
\]
The summands are iid, mean zero, square integrable by overlap and the fourth-moment envelope, and have variance \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}>0\).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:iid-central-limit}\) proves the Gaussian limit.  Equations (A4)--(A5), root-\(n\) consistency of the finite cell ratios and shares, and conditional Chebyshev imply
\[
\mathbb P_n(\widehat\phi-\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P})^2=o_P(1).
\]
Expanding the centered empirical second moment proves \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\to_PV_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Positivity of the limit places the studentizing factor within \((1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon)\) with probability tending to one for every \(\epsilon>0\); sandwiching at Gaussian continuity points proves the stated Wald coverage.  Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) identifies this variance as the published-class efficiency bound.

Fix a declared comparator and write \(b=b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\).  Both \(b\) and \(b^\star(X)\) satisfy \(A'b=\omega\).  Every coordinate of \(\Psi\) in target block \(k\) has conditional mean \(h_k(X)\), so both aggregate scores have conditional mean \(\omega'h(X)\).  Put \(d=b-b^\star=Nz\).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) gives \(N'\Gamma b^\star=0\), whence
\[
b'\Gamma b-b^{\star\prime}\Gamma b^\star
=2d'\Gamma b^\star+d'\Gamma d=d'\Gamma d=z'Hz.
\tag{E7}
\]
The conditional variance formula and integration prove (E1).  The identities
\[
V_{\mathrm{agg}}-V_{\mathrm{can}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}},
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{can}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{model}}
\]
from Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) then prove (E2)--(E3).

Moreover,
\[
N'\Gamma b=N'\Gamma(b-b^\star)=Hz.
\tag{E8}
\]
If (E8) is zero, then (E7) is zero.  Conversely, if the expectation of (E7) is zero, nonnegativity gives \(z'H(X)z=0\) almost surely.  Positive semidefiniteness implies \(H(X)z=0\), so (E8) vanishes.  This proves (E4), including singular cases.

The difference \(b'\Psi-\psi_P^0\) is a measurable clean-comparison contrast and belongs to
\[
\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp
\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp
\]
by Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\).  Therefore \(b'\Psi\) is an ambient gradient of the same target in both observed models.  An ambient gradient has variance equal to a model's canonical bound exactly when its projection onto that model's tangent orthocomplement is zero.  Tangent exhaustion gives
\[
\mathcal T_P^\perp
=\overline{\{a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\}},
\qquad
\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp
=\overline{\{a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\}}.
\tag{E9}
\]
Orthogonality to every measurable multiple in (E9) is equivalent, by conditional expectation, to (E5) and (E6), respectively.  This proves the two remaining equivalences and the interpretation of the three diagnostics.

Fix \(n\), abbreviate \(t=t_{J_n,P}\), \(G=E_P[tt']\), \(g=g_{\Delta,J_n,P}\), and \(D=D\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},P}\).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:ovs-normal-tangent-projection}\) gives
\[
t_j=\Pi_{\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}}\{v_j-E_Pv_j\}
\in\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}},
\qquad j=1,\ldots,J_n.
\tag{G10}
\]
Therefore \(\mathcal S_{J_n,P}=\{c't:c\in\mathbb R^{J_n}\}\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\).

If \(c\in\ker G\), then
\[
0=c'Gc=E_P[(c't)^2],
\]
so \(c't=0\) in \(L_2(P)\).  Linearity and well-definedness of \(D\) on \(\mathcal S_{J_n,P}\) give
\[
c'g=\sum_{j=1}^{J_n}c_jD[t_j]=D[c't]=D[0]=0.
\tag{G11}
\]
Thus \(g\in(\ker G)^\perp=\operatorname{range}G\) and \(GG^\dagger g=g\).

Put \(a=G^\dagger g\) and \(\zeta=t'a\).  For \(s=c't\in\mathcal S_{J_n,P}\), symmetry of \(G^\dagger\) and (G11) yield
\[
E_P[\zeta s]=a'Gc=g'G^\dagger Gc=g'c=D[s].
\tag{G12}
\]
If \(\widetilde\zeta\) is another representer in the same space, use \(s=\widetilde\zeta-\zeta\) in both representer identities to obtain
\(E_P[(\widetilde\zeta-\zeta)^2]=0\).  Hence the representer is unique in \(L_2(P)\).  Finally,
\[
E_P[\zeta^2]
=g'G^\dagger GG^\dagger g=g'G^\dagger g.
\]
This proves every population assertion; no step controls an estimated growing-dimensional Riesz map.

The construction gives \(p_{a,s}(x)=1/6\) for every \(a\in\{2,3,\infty\}\), \(s\in\{0,1\}\), and \(x\in\{-1,1\}\), hence \(\pi_{2,1}=1/6\).  Outcomes are bounded by \(1/4\).  Consistency holds by construction.  The treatment term vanishes for \(s=0\) and before adoption, proving no ineligible effect and no anticipation.  The residual distribution depends on \((G,X)\) but not on \(S\), so every untreated eligibility gap is zero within every cohort.  Thus every global OVS conditional parallel-gap restriction holds and \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\in\mathcal M\).

The residual signs have conditional mean zero.  The three conditional DDD contrasts and both targets equal \(\delta\), so the target-cell term \(q-\theta\) in \(\Psi\) is zero.  Put \(a=3/4\).  Direct substitution into Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
(G,S)&\Psi_{(2,2),3}&\Psi_{(2,2),\infty}&\Psi_{(2,3),\infty}\\ \hline
(2,1)&aU^{\mathrm w}&aU^{\mathrm w}&aV^{\mathrm w}\\
(2,0)&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aV^{\mathrm w}\\
(3,1)&-aU^{\mathrm w}&0&0\\
(3,0)&aU^{\mathrm w}&0&0\\
(\infty,1)&0&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aV^{\mathrm w}\\
(\infty,0)&0&aU^{\mathrm w}&aV^{\mathrm w}.
\end{array}
\tag{Q1}
\]
Every row has conditional probability \(1/6\), and
\[
E[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=2]
=E[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=3]=0,
\quad
E[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=\infty]=xr.
\]
Multiplying (Q1) row by row proves
\[
\Gamma(x)=\frac{3}{16}
\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\1&2&xr\\0&xr&2\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{Q2}
\]

Feasibility is \(b_1+b_2=\omega_1\), \(b_3=\omega_2\), so write
\(b(q)=(\omega_1/2+q,\omega_1/2-q,\omega_2)'\).  Equation (Q2) gives
\[
\frac{d}{dq}\{b(q)'\Gamma(x)b(q)\}=\frac{3}{16}(4q-2xr\omega_2),
\qquad
\frac{d^2}{dq^2}\{b(q)'\Gamma(x)b(q)\}=\frac34>0.
\]
Thus \(q^\star(x)=xr\omega_2/2\).  Also
\[
\det\!\left(
\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\1&2&xr\\0&xr&2\end{pmatrix}-\lambda I\right)
=(2-\lambda)\{(2-\lambda)^2-(1+r^2)\}.
\]
This proves the eigenvalue formula, and \(r^2<7/9\) makes the smallest strictly larger than \((3/16)(2-4/3)=1/8\).

Because \(E[X]=0\), the unconditional covariance in (Q2) has zero entries coupling the first target block with the third score.  Both the joint constant program and the first OVS block are uniquely minimized at \(q=0\), while the third coordinate is fixed.  Hence both comparator rules return \((\omega_1/2,\omega_1/2,\omega_2)'\).  Their displacement from \(b^\star(X)\) is \((-Xr\omega_2/2,Xr\omega_2/2,0)'\), so
\[
E_P[(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star)'\Gamma(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star)]
=\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}.
\tag{Q3}
\]
The conditional quadratic has second derivative \(3/4\) and minimizer \(Xr\omega_2/2\); therefore an arbitrary constant \(q\) has integrated excess
\[
\frac38E[(q-Xr\omega_2/2)^2]
=\frac{3q^2}{8}+\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}.
\tag{Q4}
\]

For the published OVS model, at period two the clean set is \(\{3,\infty\}\), producing the single nonzero row \((2,3,\infty)\); at period three the clean set is \(\{\infty\}\), producing no row.  The localized model also has exactly the period-two row, obtained from the target \((2,2)\) and the common-cohort pair with \((2,3)\).  The deterministic lexicographic conventions and the identical residual formulas therefore give
\[
Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}=Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}=Z_{2;3,\infty}.
\tag{Q5}
\]
The kernel of \(A'\) is spanned by \((1,-1,0)'\), and direct subtraction in (Q1), remembering that the target-share corrections cancel within the first block, gives
\[
R_{(2,2),3}-R_{(2,2),\infty}=-Z_{2;3,\infty}.
\tag{Q6}
\]
Equations (Q5)--(Q6) and tangent exhaustion in Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) prove
\[
\mathcal C_P=\mathcal T_P^\perp=\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp.
\]
Hence both projection increments vanish: \(\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{model}}=0\).  Proposition \(\ref{prop:equality-frontier}\) turns (Q3)--(Q4) into losses relative to \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Substitution of \(r=\omega_2=1/2\) gives \(3/512\).

If every \(\mathcal J_k\) is a singleton, then \(M=K_0\), and under the fixed target ordering the incidence matrix \(A\) is the identity.  Thus \(\ker(A')=\{0\}\), \(N\) has no columns, and \(A'b=\omega\) has one solution.  The conditional and constant loading programs coincide.

If \(X\) is degenerate, \(\Gamma(X)=\Gamma\) almost surely.  The identity \(E_P[\Psi\mid X]=Ah(X)\) and total covariance give
\[
\Omega=E_P[\Gamma(X)]+\operatorname{Var}_P\{Ah(X)\}=\Gamma,
\]
because the last variance vanishes.  Hence the conditional and constant quadratic programs have the same objective.  Write \(b=b^0+Nz\).  Since \(b^0\in\operatorname{col}A\) and \(Nz\in\ker A'\), the two terms are Euclidean-orthogonal.  Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) selects \(z=-H^\dagger N'\Gamma b^0\) in \(\operatorname{range}H\), which is the minimum-Euclidean-norm solution of the normal equations and therefore is the Moore--Penrose convention defining \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\).

Finally, Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) shows that a loaded pairwise score is canonical only after the published normal equation is verified.  Thus the stated absence of an unsupported external influence-function identification follows.

Fix \(k=(g,t)\), write \(c=c_0(k)\), and put \(\mu_k=E_P[p_{g,1}(X)q_{k,c}(X)]\), so \(\theta_k=\mu_k/\pi_{g,1}\).  Overlap bounds every inverse propensity, while the fourth-moment assumption and Jensen's inequality give the integrability needed to differentiate the finite sums and expectations along a regular dominated submodel.

Writing a dot for a derivative at zero, quotient differentiation gives
\[
\dot p_{a,v}(x)=E_P[(\mathbf 1_{a,v}-p_{a,v}(x))s(O)\mid X=x]
\tag{R1}
\]
and
\[
\dot m_{a,v,u}(x)
=\frac{E_P[\mathbf 1_{a,v}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{a,v,u}(x)\}s(O)\mid X=x]}{p_{a,v}(x)}.
\tag{R2}
\]
Differentiating \(\mu_k\) gives
\[
\dot\mu_k=E_P[p_{g,1}q_{k,c}s]+E_P[\dot p_{g,1}q_{k,c}]+E_P[p_{g,1}\dot q_{k,c}].
\tag{R3}
\]
The first two terms combine, by (R1) and iterated expectation, to \(E_P[\mathbf 1_{g,1}q_{k,c}s]\).  For example, the \(m_{g,0,u}\) contribution from (R2) is
\[
-E_P\!\left[\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{p_{g,0}(X)}\mathbf 1_{g,0}
\{\Delta Y_u-m_{g,0,u}(X)\}s(O)\right],
\]
and the other three cell contributions have the signs in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\).  Summing over \(u\) gives
\[
\dot\mu_k=E_P[\pi_{g,1}R_{k,c,P}(O)s(O)].
\tag{R4}
\]
Also \(\dot\pi_{g,1}=E_P[\mathbf 1_{g,1}s]\), since \(E_P[s]=0\).  Because \(\pi_{g,1}>0\), another quotient rule gives
\[
\dot\theta_k
=\frac{\dot\mu_k-\theta_k\dot\pi_{g,1}}{\pi_{g,1}}
=E_P\!\left[\left\{R_{k,c,P}-\frac{\theta_k}{\pi_{g,1}}\mathbf 1_{g,1}\right\}s\right]
=E_P[\Psi_{k,c,P}s].
\tag{R5}
\]
The bracket has mean zero because \(E_P[R_{k,c,P}]=\theta_k\).  Multiplying by fixed \(\omega_k\) and summing over finite \(\mathcal K\) proves the claim.

Apply the conditional projection calculation with \(Z=Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\), \(K=K_P\), and \(r_v(X)=E_P[Zv^0\mid X]\).  If \(a\in\ker K(X)\), then
\[
0=a'K(X)a=E_P[(a'Z)^2\mid X],
\]
so \(a'Z=0\) conditionally almost surely and \(a'r_v(X)=0\).  Hence \(r_v(X)\in\operatorname{range}K(X)\) and \(KK^\dagger r_v=r_v\).  For every measurable \(c\) with \(c(X)'Z\in L_2(P)\),
\[
E_P[\{v^0-r_v'K^\dagger Z\}c(X)'Z]
=E_P[c(X)'\{r_v-KK^\dagger r_v\}]=0.
\]
With \(c=K^\dagger r_v\), expansion of \(E_P[(v^0-c'Z)^2\mid X]\ge0\) gives
\[
r_v'K^\dagger r_v\le E_P[(v^0)^2\mid X].
\]
Since \(E_P[(r_v'K^\dagger Z)^2\mid X]=r_v'K^\dagger r_v\), the projected term is square integrable.  Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) identifies the closure of measurable multiples of \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) with \(\mathcal T_P^\perp\).  The subtracted term is therefore \(\Pi_{\mathcal T_P^\perp}v^0\), and the residual is \(\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}v^0\), as claimed.  Under the corrected Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\), the dictionary instead uses \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Repeating the same kernel, range, and orthogonality calculation with \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\), and using the published normal identity in Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\), places each such coordinate in \(\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\subseteq\mathcal T_P\).  This proves the final assertion under the corrected definition.

There are finitely many support points, cells, periods, OVS rows, and folds.  The support-mass and overlap bounds make every relevant training-cell count of order \(n\) in probability.  For a scalar cell variable \(W\) with finite second moment, conditional variance and Chebyshev's inequality give
\[
\widehat E_{-\ell}[W\mid G=a,S=s,X=x]-E_P[W\mid G=a,S=s,X=x]=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{N1}
\]
The global conditional fourth-moment envelope applies (N1) to increments and every product needed for a second moment.  Fixed dimension makes the maxima over support points and folds, and the \(L_4(P_X)\) norm, preserve this rate.  Therefore \(\widehat p-p\), \(\widehat m-m\), and the preliminary target ratios are all \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\).

Lemma \(\ref{lem:ovs-orthogonal-normal-signal}\) and clipping show that replacing \((p,m)\) by cell averages changes each signal in \(L_4(P)\) by \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\), while its conditional mean changes by only \(O_P(n^{-1})\).  Expanding
\(\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS}}\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS}\prime}-Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}Z^{\mathrm{OVS}\prime}\) and applying H\"older's inequality proves the \(K\) rate.  The same expansion of \(\widehat S^{\mathrm{OVS}}\widehat\psi^0-Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}\psi^0\) proves the \(r\) rate.  Shared cells create off-diagonal products, but these cross-products are averaged directly; no block-diagonal approximation is made.

At a fixed support point, the smallest positive eigenvalue of \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x)\), when present, is positive.  The finite support makes their positive minimum over \(x\) positive.  The eigenvalue variational inequality gives
\[
|\lambda_j(\widehat K(x))-\lambda_j(K(x))|
\le\|\widehat K(x)-K(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{N2}
\]
Since \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\) and \(\tau_n\to0\), (N2) separates zero from every fixed positive eigenvalue.  A union bound gives simultaneous rank recovery.

On the recovery event, all retained eigenvalues exceed half the fixed-law positive minimum.  The inverse identity
\[
\widehat K_R^{-1}-K_R^{-1}=\widehat K_R^{-1}(K_R-\widehat K_R)K_R^{-1}
\]
and the moment rates give the sharper \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) coefficient rate.  Without conditioning on recovery, every retained inverse eigenvalue is bounded by \(\tau_n^{-1}\), giving \(O_P(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n)\).  For \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), this is \(O_P(n^{-1/2+a})\), its square is \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) for \(a<1/4\), and its product with a root-\(n\) nuisance rate is \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\).

The first tangent-normal identity is equation (2) of Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:reference-score-gradient}\) gives, for every \(s\in\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\),
\[
\dot\tau_{\omega,P}[s]=E_P[\psi_P^0s].
\tag{T1}
\]
Abbreviate \(Z=Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), \(K=K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\), and \(r=r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\).  If \(v\in\ker K(x)\), then
\[
0=v'K(x)v=E_P[(v'Z)^2\mid X=x],
\]
so \(v'Z=0\) conditionally almost surely and \(v'r(x)=0\).  Therefore
\[
r(x)\in\operatorname{range}K(x),
\qquad K(x)K(x)^\dagger r(x)=r(x).
\tag{T2}
\]
The Moore--Penrose map is Borel measurable because
\[
K^\dagger=\lim_{j\to\infty}(K^2+j^{-1}I)^{-1}K.
\tag{T3}
\]
Put \(p_{mathrm{OVS},P}=r'K^\dagger Z\).  Symmetry and (T2) give
\[
E_P[p_{mathrm{OVS},P}^2\mid X]
=r'K^\dagger KK^\dagger r
=r'K^\dagger r
=E_P[\psi_P^0p_{mathrm{OVS},P}\mid X].
\tag{T4}
\]
Thus \(p_{mathrm{OVS},P}\in L_2(P)\), and for every square-integrable measurable multiple \(a(X)'Z\),
\[
E_P[(\psi_P^0-p_{mathrm{OVS},P})a(X)'Z]
=E_P[a(X)'\{r-KK^\dagger r\}]=0.
\tag{T5}
\]
Equations (T4)--(T5) and tangent exhaustion prove
\[
p_{mathrm{OVS},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp}\psi_P^0,
\qquad
\phi_{mathrm{OVS},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}}\psi_P^0.
\tag{T6}
\]
Combining (T1) and (T6) proves canonicality; taking expectations in (T4) proves (16).  Coefficient versions differing in \(\ker K(X)\) have the same product with \(Z\), so singularity creates no ambiguity.

The same calculation with \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) gives
\[
p_{mathrm{per},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P^\perp}\psi_P^0,
\qquad
\phi_{mathrm{can},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}\psi_P^0.
\tag{T7}
\]
Since \(\mathcal T_P^\perp\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp\), nested projections imply
\[
\phi_{mathrm{can},P}
=\phi_{mathrm{OVS},P}+(p_{mathrm{OVS},P}-p_{mathrm{per},P}),
\]
with orthogonal terms.  Pythagoras proves (17).  Also \(p_{mathrm{per},P}\) belongs to the published normal space, so the local gradient remains a valid published-model gradient.  It is canonical there exactly when it is orthogonal to every measurable multiple of \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), which is (18).

On the observable equality model, zero conditional residual means in Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) give
\[
E_P[\Psi_P\mid X]=Ah(X).
\tag{T8}
\]
Thus every feasible loading has conditional mean \(\omega'h(X)\), and iterated variance gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b(X)'\Psi_P\}
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{\omega'h(X)\}
+E_P[b(X)'\Gamma_P(X)b(X)].
\tag{T9}
\]
Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) gives \(A'b^\star=\omega\) and \(N'\Gamma b^\star=0\).  If \(d=b-b^\star\), then \(A'd=0\), so \(d=Nz\), and \(d'\Gamma b^\star=0\).  Expanding (T9) proves (19)--(20).

Let \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}\) put weight \(\omega_k\) on \((k,c_0(k))\).  Then \(\psi_P^0=b^{\mathrm{ref}\prime}\Psi_P\).  Because \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}-b^\star\in\operatorname{col}N\), the target-share corrections cancel within every block and
\[
p_{mathrm{agg},P}:=\psi_P^0-\phi_{mathrm{agg},P}
=(b^{\mathrm{ref}}-b^\star(X))'R_P\in\mathcal C_P.
\tag{T10}
\]
Using \(N'R=N'\Psi\), (T8), \(N'A=0\), and \(N'\Gamma b^\star=0\),
\[
E_P[N'R_P\phi_{mathrm{agg},P}\mid X]
=N'\{\Gamma_P+Ahh'A'\}b^\star=0.
\tag{T11}
\]
Therefore \(p_{mathrm{agg},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\psi_P^0\).  The nested normal spaces
\[
\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp
\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp
\]
have orthogonal successive projection increments.  Pythagoras proves (21).  Finally, orthogonality to all measurable multiples of a finite normal vector is equivalent to a zero conditional cross-moment with that vector.  Applying this to \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) and \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) proves the two equality characterizations, including (22).

added_lemmas.statement:
For any \(v\in L_2(P)\), put \(v^0=v-E_P[v]\),
\[
r_v^{\mathrm{OVS}}(X)=E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}v^0\mid X],
\qquad
t_v^{\mathrm{OVS}}=v^0-r_v^{\mathrm{OVS}}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}.
\]
At a conditional-mean interior law in the published OVS model,
\[
t_v^{\mathrm{OVS}}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}}v^0.
\]
In particular, every population coordinate of the published-normal dictionary in Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\) belongs to \(\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Abbreviate \(Z=Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), \(K=K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\), and \(r_v=r_v^{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  If \(a\in\ker K(X)\), then
\[
0=a'K(X)a=E_P[(a'Z)^2\mid X],
\]
so \(a'Z=0\) conditionally almost surely and \(a'r_v(X)=0\).  Therefore
\[
r_v(X)\in\operatorname{range}K(X),
\qquad KK^\dagger r_v=r_v.
\tag{P1}
\]
It follows that, for every measurable \(c\) for which \(c(X)'Z\in L_2(P)\),
\[
E_P[\{v^0-r_v'K^\dagger Z\}c(X)'Z]
=E_P[c(X)'\{r_v-KK^\dagger r_v\}]=0.
\tag{P2}
\]
Moreover, with \(c=K^\dagger r_v\), expansion of the nonnegative conditional square gives
\[
0\le E_P[(v^0-c'Z)^2\mid X]
=E_P[(v^0)^2\mid X]-r_v'K^\dagger r_v.
\]
Together with (P1), this gives
\[
E_P[(r_v'K^\dagger Z)^2\mid X]
=r_v'K^\dagger r_v
\le E_P[(v^0)^2\mid X],
\tag{P3}
\]
where the inequality is the finite-dimensional least-squares projection inequality.  Thus the subtracted term is square integrable.  The tangent-exhaustion identity in Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) identifies the closure of the measurable multiples of \(Z\) with \(\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp\).  Equations (P2)--(P3) therefore show that \(r_v'K^\dagger Z=\Pi_{\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp}v^0\), and the displayed residual is \(\Pi_{\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}}v^0\).  Applying this calculation to each dictionary coordinate proves the final assertion.
added_lemmas.justification: The published-bound sieve must be projected against the exhaustive OVS normal rather than the weaker localized normal.
added_lemmas.gap: The frozen localized projection lemma does not establish membership in the smaller published tangent space.
added_lemmas.consumer: The population gap-sieve theorem uses this projection coordinate by coordinate.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(z_0\in\mathbb R^d\), and let \(B_1(z),\ldots,B_L(z)\) be finitely many continuously differentiable real symmetric matrix maps near \(z_0\).  Suppose every nonzero eigenvalue of every \(B_j(z_0)\) has absolute value at least \(\kappa_0>0\).  If \(\widehat z-z_0=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), \(\tau_n\downarrow0\), and \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\), then retaining exactly the empirical eigenvalues satisfying \(|\lambda|>\tau_n\) recovers all population ranks simultaneously with probability tending to one.  On that event each thresholded inverse equals a continuously differentiable selected-rank inverse branch.  Consequently any scalar \(F\) formed by finitely many additions, multiplications, divisions by quantities nonzero at \(z_0\), and these selected-rank inverses satisfies, with \(d_0=DF(z_0)\),
\[
F_{\tau_n}(\widehat z)-F(z_0)=d_0'(\widehat z-z_0)+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\]
For a symmetric matrix coordinate \(B\), the selected-rank inverse derivative in direction \(H\) is
\[
DB_0^\sharp[H]
=-B_0^\dagger HB_0^\dagger
+(B_0^\dagger)^2H(I-B_0B_0^\dagger)
+(I-B_0^\dagger B_0)H(B_0^\dagger)^2.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
It is enough to treat one matrix because the collection is finite.  Continuous differentiability implies local Lipschitz continuity, whence
\[
\|B(\widehat z)-B(z_0)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(n^{-1/2})=o_P(\tau_n).
\tag{S1}
\]
For symmetric matrices, the min--max characterization of ordered eigenvalues gives
\[
\max_k|\lambda_k\{B(\widehat z)\}-\lambda_k\{B(z_0)\}|
\le\|B(\widehat z)-B(z_0)\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{S2}
\]
On an event whose probability tends to one, (S1)--(S2), \(\tau_n<\kappa_0/2\), and \(\|B(\widehat z)-B(z_0)\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\tau_n\) place every empirical eigenvalue from the zero cluster below \(\tau_n\) in absolute value and every empirical eigenvalue from a nonzero cluster above \(\kappa_0/2>\tau_n\).  This proves simultaneous rank recovery.

To construct the differentiable branch, choose a positively oriented contour \(\gamma\) enclosing zero and no nonzero eigenvalue of \(B_0=B(z_0)\).  For \(z\) near \(z_0\), define
\[
P_0(z)=\frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm i}\int_\gamma(wI-B(z))^{-1}\,dw.
\tag{S3}
\]
The resolvent identity
\[
(wI-B_1)^{-1}-(wI-B_2)^{-1}
=(wI-B_1)^{-1}(B_1-B_2)(wI-B_2)^{-1}
\tag{S4}
\]
shows that \(P_0(z)\) is continuously differentiable.  On an orthonormal eigenbasis of a symmetric \(B(z)\), the integral in (S3) is one for eigenvalues inside \(\gamma\) and zero for eigenvalues outside, by direct integration of \((w-\lambda)^{-1}\); hence it projects onto the eigenvalue cluster emanating from the null space.  Set
\[
B^\sharp(z)=(I-P_0(z))\{B(z)+P_0(z)\}^{-1}(I-P_0(z)).
\tag{S5}
\]
The matrix inverted in (S5) is nonsingular near \(z_0\), so (S4) makes \(B^\sharp\) continuously differentiable.  It equals \(B_0^\dagger\) at \(z_0\), and on the rank-recovery event it is the inverse that zeros the small cluster and inverts the retained eigenvalues.

Differentiating (S3)--(S5), or equivalently the four Moore--Penrose equations on the selected-rank branch, gives
\[
DB_0^\sharp[H]
=-B_0^\dagger HB_0^\dagger
+(B_0^\dagger)^2H(I-B_0B_0^\dagger)
+(I-B_0^\dagger B_0)H(B_0^\dagger)^2.
\tag{S6}
\]
Ordinary division is continuously differentiable wherever its denominator is nonzero.  The chain rule therefore makes the stated finite composition \(F\) differentiable, and its first-order expansion at \(z_0\), together with \(\widehat z-z_0=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), gives the asserted expansion.  Rank recovery makes the thresholded and selected-branch maps agree with probability tending to one.
added_lemmas.justification: The finite-support gap functional contains positive-semidefinite normal matrices and indefinite comparator KKT matrices, so its operational derivative must threshold by absolute eigenvalue.
added_lemmas.gap: An ordinary inverse delta method does not cover redundant score coordinates.
added_lemmas.consumer: The fixed-support gap theorem uses the selected-rank derivative and simultaneous rank recovery.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix a conditional-mean interior law \(P\) in the published OVS model.  Suppose \(X\) has fixed finite support with every support mass bounded below, retained-cell overlap and the fourth-moment condition hold, and \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed.  For a declared rule \(z\in\{\mathrm{OVS},\mathrm{const}\}\), let \(b_z(P)\) be the law-dependent comparator, define \(\mu(P)\), \(F_z\), and \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}\) by Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\), and take \(\tau_n\downarrow0\) with \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\).  Let
\[
d_z=DF_z^\sharp\{\mu(P)\},
\qquad
\xi_z(O)=d_z'[U(O)-\mu(P)],
\qquad
V_{\Delta,z}=E_P[\xi_z(O)^2].
\]
If \(V_{\Delta,z}>0\), then
\[
F_z\{\mu(P)\}=\operatorname{Var}_P\{b_z(P)'\Psi_P(O)\}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P),
\tag{W1}
\]
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_z(O_i)+o_P(1)
\ \Rightarrow\ N(0,V_{\Delta,z}),
\tag{W2}
\]
and \(\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}\to_PV_{\Delta,z}\).  Hence the two-sided Wald interval has pointwise asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\).  If additionally \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)\ge\delta_0>0\), its lower endpoint is at least \(\delta_0/2\) with probability tending to one.  These conclusions are pointwise; they are not uniform at an equality or rank-changing boundary.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write the support as \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_D\}\).  By the separate coordinates in (G4),
\[
P(X=x_d)=E_P[U_d^X].
\tag{W3}
\]
For every retained cell with positive probability, (G4)--(G5) give
\[
P(G=a,S=s\mid X=x_d)
=\frac{E_P[U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}]}{E_P[U_d^X]},
\qquad
E_P[\Delta Y_u\mid G=a,S=s,X=x_d]
=\frac{E_P[U^{(1,u)}_{d,a,s}]}{E_P[U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}]},
\tag{W4}
\]
and
\[
E_P[\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v\mid G=a,S=s,X=x_d]
=\frac{E_P[U^{(2,u,v)}_{d,a,s}]}{E_P[U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}]}.
\tag{W5}
\]
The support-mass bound and retained-cell overlap make every denominator in (W4)--(W5) positive.  Because \(T\), \(\mathcal G\), and the support are finite, these formulas reconstruct all first and second cross-moments used by \(\Psi\), \(\Omega\), \(Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), \(K_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), and \(r_{\mathrm{OVS}}\).

The corrected score has mean zero, so the comparator variance is
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b_z(P)'\Psi_P\}
=b_z\{\mu(P)\}'\Omega\{\mu(P)\}b_z\{\mu(P)\}.
\tag{W6}
\]
The canonical-gradient theorem and the definition of \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}\) give
\[
V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2]
-E_P[r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)]
\]
\[
=b^{\mathrm{ref}\prime}\Omega\{\mu(P)\}b^{\mathrm{ref}}
-\sum_{d=1}^DP(X=x_d)
r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)^\dagger r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d).
\tag{W7}
\]
Subtracting (W7) from (W6) is exactly (G6), which proves (W1).  This calculation also proves that the declared comparator is the rule \(b_z(P)\): its derivative includes the derivative of \(\Omega(P)\), rather than treating a numerical loading as fixed.

The fourth-moment assumption, the bound \(|\Delta Y_u|^4\le8(|Y_u|^4+|Y_{u-1}|^4)\), and the inequality
\(2|ab|\le a^2+b^2\) imply
\[
E_P[(U^{(2,u,v)}_{d,a,s})^2]
\le\tfrac12E_P[\mathbf 1_{d,a,s}\{(\Delta Y_u)^4+(\Delta Y_v)^4\}]<\infty.
\tag{W8}
\]
All other coordinates of \(U\) also have finite second moments.  Chebyshev's inequality applied coordinate by coordinate, and finiteness of \(d_\mu\), therefore give
\[
\widehat\mu-\mu=O_P(n^{-1/2}),
\qquad \Sigma_U=\operatorname{Var}_P\{U(O)\}<\infty.
\tag{W9}
\]

At the fixed law, the finitely many nonzero eigenvalues of the matrices \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)\) and of the symmetric comparator KKT matrices have a strictly positive minimum absolute value.  Each matrix entry is a differentiable rational function of \(\mu\) on the overlap domain.  Lemma \(\ref{lem:fixed-support-selected-rank-delta}\), applied with \(z=\mu\), proves simultaneous rank recovery and
\[
F_{z,\tau_n}(\widehat\mu)-F_z(\mu)
=d_z'(\widehat\mu-\mu)+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{W10}
\]
Combining (W9)--(W10) gives the expansion in (W2), and Lemma \(\ref{lem:iid-central-limit}\) applied directly to \(\xi_z\), together with \(V_{\Delta,z}>0\), gives its normal limit.

The selected-branch derivative is continuous, so rank recovery and \(\widehat\mu\to_P\mu\) imply \(\widehat d_z\to_Pd_z\).  To verify the required law of large numbers using only integrability, fix any entry \(W=U_jU_k\) and truncate it to \(W_M=W\mathbf 1\{|W|\le M\}\).  Chebyshev's inequality applies to bounded \(W_M\), while Markov's inequality gives
\[
P\{\mathbb P_n|W-W_M|>\epsilon\}
\le \epsilon^{-1}E_P[|W|\mathbf 1\{|W|>M\}],
\]
which tends to zero after first taking \(n\to\infty\) and then \(M\to\infty\).  The number of entries is finite, so
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{U(O_i)-\widehat\mu\}\{U(O_i)-\widehat\mu\}'
\longrightarrow_P\Sigma_U.
\tag{W11}
\]
Premultiplication and postmultiplication by \(\widehat d_z\) prove
\(\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}\to_Pd_z'\Sigma_Ud_z=V_{\Delta,z}\).  Since this limit is positive, for every \(\epsilon>0\) the studentizing factor lies in \((1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon)\) with probability tending to one; sandwiching its distribution between the Gaussian limits at the corresponding rescaled continuity points proves the stated pointwise Wald coverage.  Finally, (W2) implies \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)+O_P(n^{-1/2})\), while variance consistency makes the Wald half-width \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\).  If \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)\ge\delta_0\), the lower endpoint is therefore at least \(\delta_0/2\) with probability tending to one.
added_lemmas.justification: This closes pointwise inference for the published-bound efficiency gap in the same discrete-covariate regime used by the attaining estimator.
added_lemmas.gap: The result is pointwise away from zero variance, equality, and rank-changing boundaries; it does not claim a continuous-covariate growing-sieve remainder.
added_lemmas.consumer: The optional \(\texttt{triplediff}\) backend may expose the plug-in gap estimate, standard error, and Wald interval only in the certified fixed-support branch.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For either \(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\in\{b^{\mathrm{OVS}},b^{\mathrm{const}}\}\),
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P(O)\}-V_{\mathrm{agg}}
=E_P[(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star(X))'\Gamma_P(X)(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star(X))].
\tag{E1}
\]
Its losses relative to the localized and published bounds are, respectively,
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P(O)\}-V_{\mathrm{can}}
=E_P[(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star)'\Gamma_P(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star)]
+\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}(P),
\tag{E2}
\]
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P(O)\}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star)'\Gamma_P(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^\star)]
+\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}(P)+\Delta_{\mathrm{model}}(P).
\tag{E3}
\]
Equality with the aggregate score-family optimum holds if and only if
\[
N'\Gamma_P(X)b^{\mathrm{cmp}}=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{E4}
\]
Equality with the localized-model bound holds if and only if
\[
E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\{b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\}\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely},
\tag{E5}
\]
and equality with the published OVS bound holds if and only if
\[
E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\{b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\}\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.

The conditional eigenvalues are \(3/8\) and \(3\{2\pm\sqrt{1+r^2}\}/16\), so the smallest exceeds \(1/8\).  Both constant comparators equal \((\omega_1/2,\omega_1/2,\omega_2)'\), and
\[
\Delta(b^{\mathrm{OVS}})=\Delta(b^{\mathrm{const}})
=\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}>0.
\]
Every deterministic feasible loading has the form \(b(q)=(\omega_1/2+q,\omega_1/2-q,\omega_2)'\) and satisfies
\[
\Delta\{b(q)\}=\frac{3q^2}{8}+\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}.
\]
In this architecture the deterministic row conventions give
\[
Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}=Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}=Z_{2;3,\infty},
\qquad
\mathcal C_P=\mathcal T_P^\perp=\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp.
\]
Consequently \(\Delta_{\mathrm{normal}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{model}}=0\), so every displayed loss is relative to the published OVS semiparametric bound.  At \(r=\omega_2=1/2\), the exact published-bound gain is \(3/512\).

prose_updates.interpretation: There are three precision frontiers.  Conditional loading by \(b^\star(X)\) minimizes variance within the aggregate pairwise-score family.  Projection against \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) gives the larger localized model's bound.  Projection against the exhaustive \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) gives the smaller published bound.  A comparator reaches these frontiers when, respectively, \(N'\Gamma_P(X)b^{\mathrm{cmp}}=0\), \(E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\mid X]=0\), and \(E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\mid X]=0\). The published-normal finite-sieve characterization does not establish a growing-sieve remainder for continuous covariates.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The note covers a fixed finite horizon and target set at interior laws admitting a full-data extension in the global OVS model. The \(3/512\) witness is genuinely relative to the published bound because all three normal closures coincide.  No continuous-covariate gap Wald theorem, equality-boundary inference, or rank-uniform guarantee is claimed.
